questions.question: List the vector (genus-level or common name) associated with each of the following infections.
questions.question_raw: List the vector (genus-level or common name) associated with the following infection:
questions.model_answer:
a) Aedes mosquito (Aedes aegypti/albopictus).
b) Anopheles mosquito.
c) Triatomine (reduviid, "kissing") bug.
d) Rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the Anopheles vector of malaria is stated in this chapter (p. 3319); the Aedes, triatomine-bug, and rat-flea vectors are from standard knowledge.

questions.question: Name the vector (genus or common name) for each of the following diseases.
questions.question_raw: Name the vector of the disease (genus or common name).
questions.model_answer:
a) Dengue virus: Aedes mosquito (Aedes aegypti/albopictus).
b) Falciparum malaria: female Anopheles mosquito.
c) Trypanosoma cruzi: triatomine (reduviid) "kissing" bug.
d) Endemic (murine) typhus: rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis).
questions.beyond_mandell: Only the mosquito vector of dengue is in this chapter (Table 317.1, p. 3815); Anopheles/malaria, triatomine/T. cruzi, and rat flea/murine typhus rest on standard Mandell/CDC knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: Dengue virus - Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus. Falciparum malaria - female Anopheles spp. Trypanosoma cruzi - Triatomine insect ('kissing' bug). Endemic Murine Typhus - Xenopsylla cheopis (Rat flea)

questions.question: Name seven tropical infections that can be diagnosed with a peripheral blood smear (Giemsa).
questions.question_raw: Trivia: Seven tropical infections that can be diagnosed with peripheral blood smear (Giemsa)
questions.model_answer: (1) Malaria (Plasmodium spp.). (2) Babesiosis. (3) Filariasis (microfilariae). (4) Relapsing fever (Borrelia recurrentis - louse-borne; and tick-borne Borrelia). (5) African trypanosomiasis. (6) American trypanosomiasis (Trypanosoma cruzi/Chagas). (7) Bartonellosis (Bartonella bacilliformis, Oroya fever).
questions.beyond_mandell: This malaria chapter notes only malaria, Babesia, filaria, and Borrelia recurrentis as visible on thin smear (p. 3310); trypanosomes and Bartonella bacilliformis are added from standard tropical-medicine knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: African/American trypanosomiasis, Babesia, Bartonella (bacilliformis - Oroya fever), Filariasis, Malaria, TBRF (tick-borne relapsing fever), LBRF (louse-borne relapsing fever) (also Histoplasmosis, Leptospirosis mentioned)
